title: Compatible geometric direct-image fibre comparisons
statement: Let f:X->S and fi:Xi->S (i in Fin n) be proper, flat and locally finitely presented, with ui:Xi->X and ui;f=fi. Let L be an invertible module on X. Let k:W->S be an immersion, w in W, s=k(w), and tau identify the pullback of L to X_s with O_X_s. Put E=R(f_W)_*(L_W[0]) and Ei=R(fi_W)_*((ui^*L)_W[0]), where the subscript W denotes base change along k. Then there exists one comparison from the derived residue fibre of the source direct image E to H1(X_s,O). For each index i there exists a comparison for Ei such that the map under derivedFiberCohomologyFunctor of the canonical `picardDerivedCoefficientMap` [new-picard-derived-coefficient-map] intertwines these comparisons with structureSheafCohomologyPullback along ui_s. The source comparison is shared by the whole finite family; n may be zero.

proof.text: Use the already constructed picardDerivedCoefficientMap. It is the coefficient pullback adjunction unit, canonical single-module pullback map and normalized direct-image composition; its two projection equations identify the target coefficient. No affine model or representative is needed.

Apply arbitrary base change to the invertible source and target coefficients. Canonical single-pullback composition identifies the coefficient square; derivedBaseChange_source_transport identifies the maps after residue pullback.

An immersion gives an isomorphism of residue fields. Pullback pasting identifies the iterated fibres with X_s and Xi_s, compatibly with ui. Transport tau and its pullbacks using the same source trivialization. Use field-base cohomology with comparisons normalized on common injective resolution section complexes. Derived adjunction units then give the ordinary coefficient pullback maps, rather than arbitrary objectwise equivalences.

For structure coefficients use the explicit unit-to-abelian comparison and its pullback naturality to identify these maps with structureSheafCohomologyPullback. Their normalized isomorphisms give the source and target comparisons and the equation for all i.
